correctness.rationale: For distinct vertices the pair type is the adjacency bit plus the achievable Boolean adjacency patterns of a third distinct vertex. Equality choices are always retained and a repeated pair sees just neighbor/nonneighbor existence. When h≥3 (and also when h=2,b≥3), the order exceeds 2b+4, so two closed neighborhoods leave an outside nonneighbor. A common neighbor is unique and exists exactly at distance two; at distance one or two, the one-sided pattern occurs exactly at a nonleaf endpoint, and at distance at least three both one-sided patterns occur. For h≥3 every vertex sees a distance-at-least-three vertex; each internal vertex sees nonleaves at distances one and two. The leaf, its parent, its grandparent, and higher internal vertices have the four asserted possibilities for their own status and nearby leaves, all realized, giving constant pointed-type sets. At height two the corresponding root, middle and leaf profiles are constant for b≥3, with the root having no distance-three vertex. At height one the center and leaf profiles stabilize once there is a third leaf. The singleton, universal vertex and radius-at-most-two sentences distinguish the height regions, and an independent triple or a dominating pair distinguishes the binary exceptions at heights one or two respectively. The tall class has minimum order 15. In a nontrivial tree, distinct equal-open-neighborhood vertices cannot have two common neighbors and so must be leaves at one parent; three such leaves exist exactly for b≥3. This validates the rank-four witness without implying a full rank-four classification.
residual_risks: The finite projection alone is not an extrapolation beyond the test cases; its use for all parameters requires the published directed classification, or the frozen structural proof as checked separately.

The remaining rank-four example is a direct open-neighborhood fact, not a new cutoff or full rank-four classification.
